newsitem.title: USA: Boeing worried by EU, U.S. subsidy talk - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing worried by EU, U.S. subsidy talk - WSJ.

text.p: European Union and U.S. officials have begun talks on European complaints about U.S. aircraft maker subsidies and Boeing fears the outcome will be linked to an EU decision on its planned takeover of McDonnell Douglas, the Wall Street Journal said.

According to U.S. trade officials, the pending EU decision on the merger was not discussed in the first session of subsidy talks which opened Thursday, the newspaper said in its electronic edition on Monday.
But people familiar with Boeing's position say the firm is worried the timing of EU complaints will join a European merger decision to the outcome of talks, the Journal said.
In 1992 Trans-Atlantic talks on the matter, Europe's Airbus Industrie and Boeing each said the other countries unfairly supported their native aircraft makers, the Journal said.
The newspaper said the subject would come up when U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan meet this weekend in Toronto to trade talks.
